Mortal
môr´tal
adj. (subject to death; of the body, dying; rendering Greek thnetos, Hebrew enosh)
Latin mortalis, from mors, death. Paul's thnetos is used only of the body; the Bible's mortal is flesh that will die, and its immortality is that flesh raised.

Biblical Definition

“For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality” (1Co 15:53), and when it has, “then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory” (1Co 15:54). “If the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you” (Rom 8:11). “Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body” (Rom 6:12). Paul's ministry: “that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh” (2Co 4:11). Eliphaz: “Shall mortal man be more just than God?” (Job 4:17). Asa: “let not man prevail against thee” — mortal man (2Ch 14:11).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines mortal as subject to death; destined to die; deadly, destructive to life; and, as a noun, a man, a being subject to death.

expand to see more

MORTAL, a. Subject to death; destined to die. Man is mortal.

2. Deadly; destructive to life; causing death, or that must cause death; as a mortal wound; mortal poison.

3. Bringing death; final; as mortal agony.

MORTAL, n. A man; a being subject to death.

Key Scripture

1Co 15:53 — "For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality."

1Co 15:54 — "So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory."

Rom 8:11 — "But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you."

Rom 6:12 — "Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof."

2Co 4:11 — "For we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus' sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh."

Job 4:17 — "Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?"

Modern Corruption

Immortality is preached as the soul escaping the body, and Paul says this mortal must put on immortality.

expand to see more

The Greek hope was the soul's release from a mortal body; the Christian hope is the mortal body clothed. First Corinthians 15:53 does not say the mortal shall be shed but that this mortal — Paul is pointing at himself — must put on immortality, as a man puts on a garment over what he already is. The resurrection is the doctrine, and the funeral talk of a soul finally free of the body is not Christianity but Plato with hymns. Romans 8:11 says whose work it will be: the Spirit who dwells in the believer now will quicken the mortal body then, so that the same Spirit is the down payment and the resurrection.

Rome divided sins into mortal and venial — those that kill grace in the soul and those that merely wound it — and built the confessional on the distinction. Scripture's mortal is never a class of sin; it is the body, and every sin is mortal in its wage, for “the wages of sin is death” without a schedule of exceptions. Romans 6:12 gives the word its only ethical use: let not sin reign in your mortal body. The body is dying, and sin would like to be king of it for the time it has left; the Christian's answer is that the body has been promised to Another.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek thnetos (G2349), liable to death, mortal; Hebrew enosh (H582), man in his frailty, mortal man.

expand to see more

Greek thnetos (G2349) — mortal; Romans 6:12, 8:11, 1 Corinthians 15:53–54, 2 Corinthians 4:11, 5:4.

Hebrew enosh (H582) — frail man, mortal; Job 4:17, 2 Chronicles 14:11, Psalm 8:4, 9:20.

Usage

"“This mortal must put on immortality” — the body clothed, not escaped."

"“Shall also quicken your mortal bodies” — the same Spirit, now and then."

"“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body” — a dying body promised to Another."
